RESULT [selftrain]: Self-training gives +1.3 to +3.4 AP across all COCO data sizes. Pre-training helps only at one-fifth of the labels and hurts with the full dataset. The best model reaches 54.3 AP, +1.5 over the strongest SpineNet.
US [selftrain]: This is the classic evidence that self-training adds gains on top of a strong supervised base. It fits the professor's order: base dataset first, pseudo-labelled increments second. The gains are modest (1-3 AP), so round-to-round changes will be near the noise level of a single training run, and the rollback gate needs repeated seeds or confidence intervals.
CORRECTION [selftrain]: Self-training gives +1.3 to +3.4 AP, and 54.3 AP is +1.5 over the strongest SpineNet (52.8). Both match. The pre-training claim is oversimplified.
